children: By Pawel Florkiewicz and Karol Badohal
Poland's central bank is in wait-and-see mode, and interest rates may remain unchanged until the middle of next year, National Bank of Poland Governor Adam Glapinski said on Thursday.
The NBP kept its main interest rate at 3.75% on Wednesday, maintaining its cautious approach as rising commodity prices and increased energy costs create a risk of higher inflation.

"I predict that interest rates will be stable for a long time. I think until the end of the year, until the middle of next year. However, if we are threatened by a trend of higher inflation, we will react immediately," Glapinski said.
"We have interest rates at the right level; they stabilize the economy, stabilize inflation. These are not high rates."
Inflation rose to 3.4% on the year in August, more than analysts expected and nearing the top end of the central bank's target range of 1.5% to 3.5%.
"We see a risk of exceeding the NBP's target, with inflation rising above 3.5% in the coming months ... Many factors will influence this. Commodity prices will remain key," Glapinski said.
The NBP governor cited factors that could influence the future path of inflation, emphasizing the role of the wage growth rate.

"We need to continue to monitor wage dynamics because, in the event of external shocks, they could have a decisive impact on inflation. Next year is an election year, and that's not conducive to wage discipline," Glapinski said.
Glapinski said in July he could propose a 25-basis-point interest rate cut after the summer.
"That is an absolutely unrealistic point of view now," he said on Thursday, adding that circumstances have changed.
